items.question: Why are you interested in Cloudflare's Software Engineering Internship? What products or features are you interested in building?
items.problem:
Expected "Most of what I've built runs on infrastructure I didn't have to think much about, and the projects where I did have to think about it are the ones that taught me the most. Building the anomaly-detection system at SAC Nexus meant owning the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI microservice, and a public detection API, and the hard part was never the model. It was latency, failure modes, and whether an alert reached a human in a form they could act on. Cloudflare runs the network layer where those constraints are the whole job, and I'd rather learn systems engineering somewhere requests are measured in millions than in a local dev environment.

The part I'd want to work on is developer-facing tooling and anything touching automation safety. I built a Playwright-based job-application agent in TypeScript where every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed environment flags and every application moves through an explicit state machine, because a single wrong browser action can submit something real. That question of where automation should stop, not just where it can go, seems directly relevant to bot management, security products, and edge compute. I also want to work somewhere an intern owns a real piece of a system rather than isolated tickets."; page shows "Undergrad"
